base_method_text.title: FiT: Flexible Vision Transformer for Diffusion Model
base_method_text.summary:
Nature is infinitely resolution-free. In the context of this reality,
existing diffusion models, such as Diffusion Transformers, often face
challenges when processing image resolutions outside of their trained domain.
To overcome this limitation, we present the Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT),
a transformer architecture specifically designed for generating images with
unrestricted resolutions and aspect ratios. Unlike traditional methods that
perceive images as static-resolution grids, FiT conceptualizes images as
sequences of dynamically-sized tokens. This perspective enables a flexible
training strategy that effortlessly adapts to diverse aspect ratios during both
training and inference phases, thus promoting resolution generalization and
eliminating biases induced by image cropping. Enhanced by a meticulously
adjusted network structure and the integration of training-free extrapolation
techniques, FiT exhibits remarkable flexibility in resolution extrapolation
generation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the exceptional performance
of FiT across a broad range of resolutions, showcasing its effectiveness both
within and beyond its training resolution distribution. Repository available at
https://github.com/whlzy/FiT.
base_method_text.main_contributions: The paper introduces Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT), a novel transformer architecture for diffusion models that generates images with unrestricted resolutions and aspect ratios. Key contributions include a flexible training pipeline that eliminates cropping, a unique transformer architecture for dynamic token length modeling using 2D RoPE, Masked MHSA and SwiGLU and a training-free resolution extrapolation method using VisionNTK and VisionYaRN for arbitrary resolution generation.
base_method_text.methodology: FiT conceptualizes images as sequences of dynamically-sized tokens, allowing adaptation to diverse aspect ratios. It employs a flexible training pipeline that preserves the original image aspect ratio. The network architecture incorporates 2D Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE), Swish-Gated Linear Unit (SwiGLU), and Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) to handle variable-length token sequences and padding tokens. Training-free extrapolation techniques like VisionNTK and VisionYaRN are tailored for 2D RoPE to enhance performance across different resolutions.
base_method_text.experimental_setup: The model is trained on the ImageNet dataset with a maximum resolution limit of HW <= 256x256. Evaluation metrics include Fre'chet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall. Experiments are conducted across various aspect ratios (1:1, 1:2, 1:3) and resolutions, both within and beyond the training distribution, to assess image synthesis and resolution extrapolation abilities.
base_method_text.limitations: The FiT-XL/2 model was trained for a limited number of steps (1.8M), and its performance at the training resolution of 256x256 is slightly inferior to DiT-XL/2, which had longer training. The generative capabilities of FiT-XL/2 with higher resolution training (larger token length limitation) haven't been thoroughly explored. The study primarily focuses on training-free resolution extrapolation techniques, without exploring methods that require additional training.
base_method_text.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring the generative capabilities of FiT with higher resolution training, investigating resolution extrapolation methods that require additional training, and further exploring the potential of FiT to handle arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios.

add_method_texts.title:
FiTv2: Scalable and Improved Flexible Vision Transformer for Diffusion
  Model
add_method_texts.summary:
\textit{Nature is infinitely resolution-free}. In the context of this
reality, existing diffusion models, such as Diffusion Transformers, often face
challenges when processing image resolutions outside of their trained domain.
To address this limitation, we conceptualize images as sequences of tokens with
dynamic sizes, rather than traditional methods that perceive images as
fixed-resolution grids. This perspective enables a flexible training strategy
that seamlessly accommodates various aspect ratios during both training and
inference, thus promoting resolution generalization and eliminating biases
introduced by image cropping. On this basis, we present the \textbf{Flexible
Vision Transformer} (FiT), a transformer architecture specifically designed for
generating images with \textit{unrestricted resolutions and aspect ratios}. We
further upgrade the FiT to FiTv2 with several innovative designs, includingthe
Query-Key vector normalization, the AdaLN-LoRA module, a rectified flow
scheduler, and a Logit-Normal sampler. Enhanced by a meticulously adjusted
network structure, FiTv2 exhibits $2\times$ convergence speed of FiT. When
incorporating advanced training-free extrapolation techniques, FiTv2
demonstrates remarkable adaptability in both resolution extrapolation and
diverse resolution generation. Additionally, our exploration of the scalability
of the FiTv2 model reveals that larger models exhibit better computational
efficiency. Furthermore, we introduce an efficient post-training strategy to
adapt a pre-trained model for the high-resolution generation. Comprehensive
experiments demonstrate the exceptional performance of FiTv2 across a broad
range of resolutions. We have released all the codes and models at
\url{https://github.com/whlzy/FiT} to promote the exploration of diffusion
transformer models for arbitrary-resolution image generation.
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper addresses the limitation of existing diffusion models in handling arbitrary image resolutions by introducing FiTv2, an improved Flexible Vision Transformer. FiTv2 conceptualizes images as sequences of tokens with dynamic sizes, enabling resolution generalization and eliminating biases from image cropping. The key contributions include architectural enhancements (Query-Key vector normalization, AdaLN-LoRA), a rectified flow scheduler, a Logit-Normal sampler, and a mixed data preprocessing strategy, resulting in faster convergence and better performance across various resolutions.
add_method_texts.methodology: FiTv2 builds upon the Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT) architecture, incorporating Query-Key Vector Normalization for training stability, AdaLN-LoRA for efficiency, a rectified flow scheduler for faster convergence, and a Logit-Normal sampler for improved timestep sampling. It also employs a mixed data preprocessing strategy, combining fixed and flexible resolution images during training. Training-free extrapolation techniques like VisionNTK and attention scaling are used for arbitrary resolution generation.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The model was trained and evaluated on the ImageNet dataset. Performance was assessed using metrics like Fre'chet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score (IS), and improved Precision and Recall. Experiments included class-guided image generation, flexible image generation, high-resolution image generation, and text-to-image generation. Evaluations were conducted on various aspect ratios and resolutions, both within and out of the training distribution.
add_method_texts.limitations: The original FiT model underperformed on the standard ImageNet 256x256 benchmark and had increased parameter count and computational costs compared to DiT. While FiTv2 improves upon FiT, specific limitations of FiTv2 itself are not explicitly stated in this paper. The paper mentions that direct extrapolation to larger resolutions outside the training distribution does not perform well without additional techniques.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring more advanced training-free extrapolation methods for arbitrary resolution generation, further scaling the FiTv2 model to investigate its scalability, and adapting the model for other image generation tasks. The paper also suggests exploring the design of more powerful diffusion transformer models inspired by this work.

base_experimental_code:
```python
from typing import Optional

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from timm.layers.mlp import SwiGLU, Mlp  
from einops import rearrange, repeat

from fit.model.rope import rotate_half
from fit.model.norms import create_norm
from fit.model.utils import modulate

class Attention(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self,
            dim: int,
            num_heads: int = 8,
            qkv_bias: bool = False,
            qk_norm: Optional[str] = None,
            attn_drop: float = 0.,
            proj_drop: float = 0.,
            rel_pos_embed: Optional[str] = None,
            add_rel_pe_to_v: bool = False,  # add relative positional embedding to value
            **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        assert dim % num_heads == 0, 'dim should be divisible by num_heads'
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        head_dim = dim // num_heads
        self.scale = head_dim ** -0.5

        self.qkv = nn.Linear(dim, dim * 3, bias=qkv_bias)
        self.q_norm = create_norm(qk_norm, head_dim)
        self.k_norm = create_norm(qk_norm, head_dim)

        self.attn_drop = nn.Dropout(attn_drop)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        self.proj_drop = nn.Dropout(proj_drop)

        self.rel_pos_embed = None if rel_pos_embed==None else rel_pos_embed.lower()
        self.add_rel_pe_to_v = add_rel_pe_to_v


    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, mask: Optional[torch.Tensor]=None,freqs_cos: Optional[torch.Tensor]=None,freqs_sin: Optional[torch.Tensor]=None) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, N, C = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x).reshape(B, N, 3, self.num_heads, C // self.num_heads).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q, k, v = qkv.unbind(0)   # B n_head N D_head
        q, k = self.q_norm(q), self.k_norm(k)

        if self.rel_pos_embed in ['rope','xpos']:  # multiplicative rel_pos_embed
            if self.add_rel_pe_to_v:
                v = v * freqs_cos + rotate_half(v) * freqs_sin
            q = q * freqs_cos + rotate_half(q) * freqs_sin
            k = k * freqs_cos + rotate_half(k) * freqs_sin

        attn_mask = mask[:, None, None, :]  # B 1 1 N
        x = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            q, k, v,
            attn_mask=attn_mask,
            dropout_p=self.attn_drop.p if self.training else 0.,
        )
        x = x.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, C)
        x = self.proj(x)
        x = self.proj_drop(x)
        return x
```

new_method:
Proposed Method (Step 3 Outcome):  
We propose a two-stage, hierarchically trained transformer framework called Hierarchical FiT-LoRA (HiFiT-LoRA). This new approach integrates the rectified flow scheduler from FiTv2 (to accelerate and stabilize training) with a novel hierarchical token strategy that addresses the Base Method’s gaps in high-resolution generalization and training inefficiencies:

1) Hierarchical Token Pipeline:  
   • During the first stage, the model operates on relatively coarse tokens to quickly learn global structure and semantic relationships.  
   • In the second stage, each coarse token is subdivided into finer tokens—enabling more detailed (and resolution-flexible) learning without re-cropping or requiring an entirely separate high-resolution training.  
   • A shared embedding ensures that both coarse and fine token representations remain consistent across stages.  

2) Rectified Flow Scheduler for Stability and Speed:  
   • Leveraging FiTv2’s rectified flow scheduler in both stages reduces the number of required diffusion steps and stabilizes learning, compensating for the potential complexity of handling hierarchical tokens.  
   • This scheduler also regularizes the transition from coarse-grained to fine-grained token representations, preventing artifacts when the model shifts to high resolutions.  

3) LoRA-Enhanced Layer Adaptation:  
   • In addition to standard FiT components, we adopt a LoRA-style lightweight parameter adaptation on the LayerNorm modules (inspired by the AdaLN-LoRA concept).  
   • This allows each training stage to load minimal learnable parameters, making the hierarchical approach significantly more memory-efficient.  

Overall, HiFiT-LoRA can smoothly handle very high resolutions, reduce training overhead, and preserve image fidelity by progressively refining representations—a distinct strategy that moves beyond incremental tweaks of the original FiT architecture.
